info.name: Karen Connect API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the Karen Connect backend, ready to try without a frontend.

**Set up:** import this file into Postman, Bruno or Insomnia. The variable `baseUrl` is `http://localhost:8000/api/v1` (the Docker stack). Open folder **0. Start here**, run **1. Log in as user1**, and carry on: the token and the ids you need are saved in the collection variables for you.

**Demo accounts** (from `docker compose up`): `user1@example.com` ... `user5@example.com`, password `password`. To act as someone else, change the `email` variable and log in again.

**Lists** are cursor-paginated: after a list request, run **Next page** to load the next one.

The full contract, with every field and every real-time event, is `docs/API.md`.

item.name: 0. Start here (run these in order)

request.description: Saves the token. Then everything else just works.

exec: console.log('Signed in as ' + json.user.name + ' (token saved in the collection variable "token")');

request.description: Checks the token.
The seeded data has two direct chats and a group. Saves `chatId`, `peerId` and `groupChatId`.

exec: if (direct) { if (direct.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('chatId', direct.id); } if (direct.other_user.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('peerId', direct.other_user.id); } }

request.description: Newest first. Saves `messageId`.
Creates a message. Run it again: a new `client_id` each time gives a new message.

exec: pm.test('message created or returned again', () => pm.expect([200, 201]).to.include(pm.response.code));
const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: The seeded data has one scheduled room, linked to the group. Saves `roomId`.
user1 is the host, so this answers `admitted` with a LiveKit token (LiveKit must be running).

item.description: With the demo data from `docker compose up`, log in as `user1@example.com` and run these seven requests top to bottom.

request.description: Create an account. It does not sign the person in: call **Log in** next. Limit: 20 per hour per IP address. If the e-mail is taken you get a 422; change it.

Exchange e-mail and password for a bearer token. **Run this first.** It saves `token` and `userId` in the collection variables, and every other request sends the token by itself.

Change the `email` variable to `user2@example.com` and log in again to act as someone else. Limit: 5 attempts a minute per e-mail and IP address.

exec: console.log('Signed in as ' + json.user.name + ' (token saved in the collection variable "token")');

request.description: Revokes this token only. Other devices stay signed in. After this, log in again.

Emails a link to reset the password, if an account uses the address. Always answers the same 200, so it never tells whether the address has an account. At most one email a minute per address. Limit: 5 a minute per IP address (shared with **Reset password**).

With `MAIL_MAILER=log` the email is written into `storage/logs/laravel.log`: copy `token` from the link into the `resetToken` variable.

Sets a new password with the token from the emailed link (works once, for 60 minutes). **Signs out every device**: log in again with the new password. A wrong or old token gives 422 with `errors.token`.
Emails a new link to verify the address (the first is sent on registration). Answers `verified: true` and sends nothing when it is verified already. Limit: 6 an hour.

What the app's `/verify-email` page sends. Copy `id`, `hash`, `expires` and `signature` from the link in the email (`storage/logs/laravel.log` with `MAIL_MAILER=log`) into the four `verify…` variables. Works without a token. 403 when the link was changed or is older than a day.
The signed-in user, with the private fields (e-mail, phone, settings).
Send only what you want to change. `settings` is merged key by key. `locale` is `en`, `my` or `ksw`.
Choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP file (max 2 MB, 6000x6000 px) in the `avatar` field of the body. SVG is refused.

Changes the password, knowing the current one. This token keeps working; **every other device is signed out**. Wrong current password: 422 with `errors.current_password`. Limit: 5 a minute.

The demo accounts all use `password`: change the `password` variable afterwards, or change it back.
Tell the server the app is open (every 30-60 seconds while visible). Marks you online. Limit: 12 a minute. Answers 204.
Presence of up to 100 people you share a chat with. Other ids are silently left out.

Most recently active first, with `latest_message`, `unread_count`, `my_membership` and `other_user` for direct chats. Saves `chatId` (a direct chat), `peerId` (the other person) and `groupChatId` in the variables.

The page size is 2 here so that you can try **Next page** with the demo data (the default is 30, the most is 100).

exec: if (direct) { if (direct.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('chatId', direct.id); } if (direct.other_user.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('peerId', direct.other_user.id); } }

request.description: After a list request, `nextUrl` holds `links.next`: send this to load the next page. If there is no next page it is empty and Postman says the URL is empty: you have reached the end.

item.name: Start or reopen a direct chat

request.description: There is only one plain direct chat between two people: 201 for a new one, 200 for the existing one.
Leave yourself out of `member_ids`: you become the owner. Saves `groupChatId`.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: One chat with its full `members` list.
Group owner or admins only.

item.name: Mark read up to a message

request.description: The read position only moves forward.
Owner or admins. 1-50 ids.
Owner only. `admin` or `member`.
Owner can remove anyone; admins can remove plain members. Answers 204.
Run this last: afterwards you are no longer in the group, so the requests above stop working for it. Direct chats cannot be left. Answers 204.

item.name: Attachments

request.description: Choose a file (max 25 MB) in the `file` field of the body. Saves `attachmentId`, and the `expires` and `signature` of its signed URL.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: No bearer token: the signature in the URL is the permission. Valid 60 minutes. Uses `expires` and `signature` saved by **Upload a file**.

item.description: Upload first: the message that uses the file is in the Messages folder.

request.description: Newest first, cursor-paginated. Saves `messageId` (the newest) and `nextUrl`.

`client_id` is your idempotency key: send the same one again and you get 200 with the original message instead of a duplicate. (Postman makes a new one on every send with `{{$guid}}`.) Limit: 30 a minute.

exec: pm.test('message created or returned again', () => pm.expect([200, 201]).to.include(pm.response.code));
const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: Replies to the message in `messageId`.

exec: pm.test('message created or returned again', () => pm.expect([200, 201]).to.include(pm.response.code));
const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: First **Upload a file** (saves `attachmentId`), then send it. `type` is `image`, `file` or `voice`.

exec: pm.test('message created or returned again', () => pm.expect([200, 201]).to.include(pm.response.code));
const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: Also the way to get fresh attachment links. For an image message it saves the thumbnail link (`thumbExpires`, `thumbSignature`) for **Download a thumbnail**.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: The thumbnail has its own signed link, different from the file's: run **Send an image message** and then **Get one message** first, which save it. Images only, and only a few moments after the upload (the thumbnail is made in the background).
The sender, within 24 hours.
The sender, or a group owner or admin. Answers 204.
Rooms that have not ended. Saves `roomId` (the first). `filter` is `hosting`, `invited` or `upcoming`.
You become the host. Saves `roomId`.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

item.name: Create a scheduled room (chat, password, waiting room)

request.description: Linking `chat_id` (here the direct chat) invites everyone in that chat and posts a message there. `scheduled_at` must be in the future: change it.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: The host and co-hosts also get `waiting_participants`.
Answers `{status: "admitted", token, livekit_url, room}` or `{status: "waiting"}`. `password` is needed only for a protected room you were not let into yet. Limit: 20 a minute.
Host or co-host. The person must have asked to join: in a room with a waiting room, log in as them (change `email`) and run **Join a room**, then log in as the host again. Otherwise 404.
Host or co-host. Only for people who are waiting (404 if they never asked to join, 409 `not_waiting` otherwise).
Host or co-host. The person must be in the room (404 otherwise). Answers 204.
`kind` is `audio` (default) or `video`. 409 `participant_not_connected` if they are not in the call.
Host only. The person must be admitted to the room (404 otherwise).
Host only.
Host only.
Host only.
What the host and co-hosts did. Host only. Cursor-paginated.

item.name: Calls

request.description: Rings the other person of the direct chat (`chatId`) for 45 seconds. Saves `callId` and `callRoomId`. `kind` is `voice` or `video`. 409 `already_in_call` / `callee_busy` when one of you is in a call; 403 for a group chat. Limit: 10 a minute.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;
if (obj) { if (obj.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callId', obj.id); } if (obj.room_id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callRoomId', obj.room_id); } }

request.description: Your ringing or ongoing call, or `{ "data": null }`. Apps ask this on start and after every reconnect. Saves `callId` when there is one.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;
if (obj) { if (obj.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callId', obj.id); } if (obj.room_id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callRoomId', obj.room_id); } }

request.description: Only the two people in it can see it (others get 404).
The caller may join while it rings; both may join once it is answered. A voice call's token publishes the microphone only.
Log in as the other person first (change `email`), then run **My current call** to get the `callId`. 409 `call_not_ringing` once it was declined, cancelled or missed.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;
if (obj) { if (obj.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callId', obj.id); } if (obj.room_id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callRoomId', obj.room_id); } }

request.description: The service worker declines with the signed `decline_url` from the incoming-call push instead, without a token.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;
if (obj) { if (obj.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callId', obj.id); } if (obj.room_id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callRoomId', obj.room_id); } }

item.name: Cancel (as the caller, while it rings)

request.description: The call becomes `missed` with `end_reason: cancelled`.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;
if (obj) { if (obj.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callId', obj.id); } if (obj.room_id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callRoomId', obj.room_id); } }

request.description: The call becomes `ended` with `end_reason: hung_up`.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;
if (obj) { if (obj.id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callId', obj.id); } if (obj.room_id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('callRoomId', obj.room_id); } }

item.description: One-to-one calls in a direct chat. Use two accounts: start as user1, then log in as the other person to accept or decline. See section 8 of docs/API.md.

item.name: Encryption: devices and keys

request.description: Needs 20-100 one-time prekeys and a signature that verifies, so this example body is rejected with a 422 on purpose: real keys must be made by a client. Shown here for the shape.

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: Your active encryption devices (public keys only).

exec: const json = pm.response.json(); const obj = json.data || json;

request.description: Needs `deviceId`: register a device first (see the folder note). Answers 204.
Needs a new id and a valid signature.
1-100 at a time.
Top up when this drops below about 10.

request.description: One bundle per active device, each with one one-time prekey that is handed out exactly once. Limit: 10 a minute per person.

item.description: The server stores public keys only. These requests need keys made by a client; see section 5 of docs/API.md.

The body is a browser's `subscription.toJSON()`. This example is refused unless the endpoint is a real push service address and the keys have the right sizes.
